Observability and Operations

Observability in TaktX is built on top of Kafka’s robust monitoring ecosystem, complemented by engine-specific metrics exposed via Prometheus. This allows operators to monitor system health, performance, and throughput in real time.

Kafka Monitoring Tools

Kafka provides a range of built-in tools and metrics for monitoring the health and performance of topics, partitions, and consumers. Key aspects to monitor include:

  • Consumer Lag: This metric shows how far behind a consumer (such as an engine node) is from the latest message in a partition. High consumer lag can indicate processing bottlenecks or resource constraints.
  • Offsets: Kafka tracks the offset of each consumer group for every partition. Monitoring offsets helps ensure that all messages are being processed and none are skipped or stuck.
  • Partition and Broker Health: Kafka exposes metrics on partition leadership, replication status, and broker availability. These are essential for ensuring high availability and fault tolerance.
  • Throughput and Latency: Kafka metrics can be used to monitor message rates, processing latency, and end-to-end throughput, helping you identify performance trends and potential issues.

These metrics can be accessed using Kafka’s built-in JMX metrics, command-line tools (such as kafka-consumer-groups.sh), and third-party monitoring solutions like Grafana and Confluent Control Center.

Prometheus Metrics

TaktX engine nodes expose detailed processing metrics via Prometheus. These metrics provide insight into:

  • Processed event counts and rates
  • Processing durations and latencies
  • State store sizes and access patterns
  • Custom business or workflow metrics (as implemented)

Prometheus metrics can be visualized and analyzed using Grafana dashboards, enabling real-time and historical analysis of engine performance.

Best Practices

  • Regularly monitor consumer lag and offsets to ensure timely processing and detect bottlenecks early.
  • Set up alerts for partition under-replication, broker failures, or high consumer lag.
  • Use Prometheus and Grafana to visualize engine-specific metrics and correlate them with Kafka-level metrics for a complete operational view.
